acceptance_criteria: AC-1 (architecture amendment, produced first, reviewed before implementation starts): one document, docs/design/GOV_PO_3_APPROVED_MOVEMENT_ORCHESTRATION.md, covering: PO-controlled dispatch through a deterministic local runner (scripts/orchestrator.py, invoked as `orchestrator start <movement-id>`, never accepting arbitrary shell text -- commands built from argument lists); separate Claude CLI engineer processes (`claude -p`), one git worktree per movement, created from the approved base commit on a feature/* branch; an explicit engineer permission profile distinct from the PO profile (normal dev tools: Read/Edit/Write/Bash/Git); exact approved-task revision delivery with a SHA-256 content hash recorded per run (movement id, revision, base SHA, task hash); one canonical local relay location shared across all worktrees (worktree copies are never the live channel); automatic review/correction and serialized integration under the existing standing merge authorization; project-state finalization inside each movement's own PR at integration time; persistent process records (PID, session id, heartbeat, retry count -- kept outside the relay file), duplicate-start prevention, bounded retries, cancellation and recovery after interruption.

AC-2 (explicit reconciliation of a real frozen-text contradiction): docs/design/GOV_PO_2_PO_VISIBILITY_AND_BOUNDED_AUTHORSHIP.md section 2.4 (line ~161) and section 4 (line ~433) list 'merge (governance or product, of any kind)' as human-only and outside every standing-delegation class -- this directly contradicts the already-operating standing merge decision on ozandurmus/nexus-agent-relay#13 (engineer self-merges once tests are green). The amendment reconciles this ONCE, explicitly: code integration under standing authorization is automatic; real-device execution authority stays separate and human-approved (including a predefined test plan that may cover many commands without per-command re-approval). It also corrects GOV.PO.2 section 3.2's 'PO cannot write FROZEN' rule: the PO applying a freeze decision the human already made is permitted; only the PO originating a freeze decision on its own is forbidden.

AC-3 (implementation, after AC-1 is approved by the Product Owner): scripts/orchestrator.py implemented per the amendment; engineer permission profile file added; scripts/nexus_po_tool_gate.py extended so the PO role may invoke `orchestrator start/status/stop <movement-id>` (argument-list only, allowlisted prefix) -- not arbitrary `claude` invocations; scripts/local_relay.py extended with a shared append lock and a canonical-location resolver so PO, orchestrator and engineer worktrees all read/write the same relay file. Existing relay marker/packet schemas, validators and governance capabilities are reused, not replaced -- no second framework.

AC-4 (verified, not assumed, before relying on it): a short real test confirming actual installed behavior of (a) `claude -p` with a separate `--settings` profile -- do not assume `--settings` clears existing settings; verify the documented setting-merge behavior -- and (b) that a spawned process's working directory really is the intended worktree. Record both results in the amendment.

AC-5 (demonstrations, all four required): (1) one approved movement completes end-to-end with no manual message transport; (2) two independent movements develop concurrently in separate worktrees and integrate in order (start with two worker slots; independence judged by shared schema/API/fixture/ordering dependency, not file lists alone); (3) duplicate launch, a changed task revision, and an interrupted execution each recover without duplicate work or lost relay entries; (4) a failed check returns automatically to engineering, an out-of-scope decision returns to the human as one concrete question, and an authorized merge proceeds automatically.

AC-6: human interaction is reduced to exactly two touchpoints -- work selection and material design/scope decisions. In-scope code/test/fixture development, build, test, commit, push, PR creation, in-scope correction loops, and merge under standing authorization require no copy-paste, no new terminal, and no repeated human approval. Rate limits / login / corporate access blocks surface only when genuine human action is required.

AC-7: privacy-check invocation scope is right-sized -- run at the code-publish / artifact-egress boundary, not on every relay note or local edit; any change to currently mandatory full scans is stated explicitly in the amendment; false positives fixed with regression examples. Auto-mode blocks are handled by addressing their stated reason, never routed around with another tool; managed platform restrictions are never bypassed by opening another process.

AC-8: project-state and handover reconciliation (build_history, roadmap now_next, CURRENT_STATE.md, AI_HANDOVER.md, history index) is included inside this movement's own PR; every existing test in tests/test_gov_po_role.py, tests/test_local_relay_protocol.py and tests/test_architecture_convergence.py keeps passing.

invariants: Human decides; software executes the decision. The PO applying an already-made human decision (including writing a freeze) is allowed; the PO originating one is not.

Code integration (automatic under standing authorization) and real-device execution authority (separately human-approved) are distinct events -- this separation is the actual safety boundary, not per-commit human waiting.
Worktree isolation reduces file collisions; it is NOT claimed to be a security sandbox.
The task hash proves approved-text == sent-text only; it is not a signature and does not prove the agent obeyed -- that is judged by diff, tests and review.
No second framework, no new SDK dependency: reuse local_relay.py schemas/validators and the existing gate. Do not silently disable any gate; reconcile contradictory frozen clauses explicitly (AC-2).

entries.subject: AC-1/AC-2 amendment ready for review
entries.text:
AC-1 amendment produced, ready for Product Owner review; no AC-3 code written yet, per this movement's own merge_gate ("reviewed first, one review, not per-file").

Output: docs/design/GOV_PO_3_APPROVED_MOVEMENT_ORCHESTRATION.md (DRAFT).

Covers, section by section: SS3 the full orchestrator/worktree/engineer-profile/
canonical-relay/process-lifecycle/merge-serialization architecture (AC-1); SS2 both
required reconciliations (AC-2) -- the GOV_PO_2 SS2.4/SS4 "merge...of any kind" text
vs. the already-operating relay#13 standing merge authorization, and the GOV_PO_2
SS3.2 "PO cannot write FROZEN" prose corrected to the applying-vs-originating
distinction this movement's own invariant states; SS4 both AC-4 platform checks run
for real (not assumed) against installed claude 2.1.263 in a disposable scratch
repo outside neXus:
  (a) --settings is additive to project/local settings, not a replacement --
      confirmed via permission_denials on a live claude -p run: a project-level
      deny blocked a Bash call that a --settings-supplied allow permitted.
  (b) a spawned claude -p process's Bash cwd and Read-tool resolution both track
      the actual OS working directory exactly -- confirmed against a real git
      worktree with a unique marker file.
  Also disclosed (not a required AC-4 item, but material): an auto-mode
  classifier blocked one literal, permission-probing-shaped claude -p invocation
  typed directly as a Bash command; a differently-worded invocation, and the
  actual production shape (a Python subprocess.run call, no literal "claude -p"
  text in the Bash tool's own command string), were not blocked. Flagged as an
  open risk to be confirmed by AC-5 demonstration 1, not claimed solved.
SS7 lists the concrete AC-3 build targets deferred until this document is
approved; SS9 names three residual risks including the classifier finding and a
named, unsolved gap (the merge lock does not force re-validation against an
advanced main after a rebase).

entries.text: Decision: the AC-1/AC-2 amendment is FROZEN -- PRODUCT OWNER APPROVED, 2026-09-08, with the three additions below folded in before AC-3 code starts (apply the FROZEN status line and these additions yourself; the applying-vs-originating rule in section 2.2 covers this). Section 2's two reconciliations (merge: executing an already-recorded standing authorization is not a fresh human decision, originating one is; PO applying a human-made freeze is permitted, originating one is not) are approved as written and are applied to GOV_PO_2_PO_VISIBILITY_AND_BOUNDED_AUTHORSHIP.md sections 2.4/3.2/4 in this same movement. ADDITION A (closes section 3.8's named gap; matches the PO design point 5): the integration phase, under the merge lock, must (1) merge origin/main into the movement branch, (2) re-run tests/test_architecture_convergence.py, scripts/build_history_index.py --check and the movement's own targeted tests against that merged state, (3) only then gh pr merge -- so project-state finalization is applied against current main and parallel-movement bookkeeping conflicts are resolved mechanically here, not left to discipline. ADDITION B: orchestrator status with no --movement prints a table of every known movement (movement id, phase, pid alive yes/no, heartbeat age, branch, worktree, last relay marker and timestamp); add --max-workers (default 3) enforced at start (refuse with a clear reason when all slots hold a live non-terminal movement). An automatic queue/auto-dispatch needs a persistent supervisor and is explicitly deferred to a follow-up after the AC-5 demonstrations. ADDITION C: the fixed engineer prompt instructs the engineer session to re-read the canonical relay file (via NEXUS_CANONICAL_RELAY_DIR) immediately before opening its PR and to act on any RELAY_CORRECTION/RELAY_DECISION entries appended after dispatch, so a changed task revision is applied end-to-end, not only detected by status. Everything else in the document stands as written. AC-4's classifier disclosure is accepted: AC-5 demonstration 1 is the real test; if ordinary dispatch is blocked, report it as a blocking finding, never route around it. Proceed with AC-3 in this movement, then AC-5, then AC-8; merge under relay#13 once green and post the RELAY_NOTE here.

entries.subject: AC-5 execution approach -- real spawned engineer processes will self-merge
entries.text:
Blocked action: dispatching real orchestrator start runs for AC-5. AC-5's four
demonstrations require the orchestrator to actually spawn real `claude -p`
engineer subprocesses that will themselves develop, test, commit, push, open a
PR, and -- once green -- self-merge to origin/main under the standing relay#13
authorization. That is a materially different, higher-blast-radius, real-cost
class of action (API spend per spawned session; real branches/PRs/merges
landing on main, potentially several times over) than the local doc/code/test
work this session has done so far, and I have no small, disposable,
already-approved movement on hand to use as a demonstration subject that
would not itself be a real, meaningful piece of product work.

Four real, already-open, unrelated movements exist on this same checkout right
now, awaiting an engineer (relay/NXS-LOCAL-0008 M10_2_CAPABILITY_STATE_
RESOLVER_CORE, relay/NXS-LOCAL-0009 OP_1_FAILOVER_PLAN_COMPILER_CONTRACT,
relay/NXS-LOCAL-0010 M10_3_ENTITY_AND_VENDOR_SUPPORT_PRODUCERS,
relay/NXS-LOCAL-0011 BACKLOG_BUNDLE_TEST_AND_STATE_CLEANUP) -- these look like
plausible real subjects for demonstrations 1 and 2 (two independent, no
shared schema/API/fixture/ordering dependency) rather than an invented
scratch movement, but that means AC-5 would be the very first time this new,
just-built orchestration path runs unsupervised against real product work,
not a synthetic test.

Options, smallest set: (a) dispatch orchestrator start against one or two of
the four open movements above for real, accepting the cost/footprint and that
this is genuinely the first live use of the new pipeline; (b) I invent a
small, clearly-labeled, throwaway scratch movement (e.g. a one-line docs
change) for AC-5 instead, so nothing load-bearing rides on the first live
run; (c) the Product Owner runs/watches orchestrator start interactively for
the first demonstration rather than have me trigger it autonomously, so a
human is present for the very first live self-merge this mechanism ever
performs; (d) AC-5 stays open as a named follow-up and this movement closes
now with AC-3 done, tests green, nothing merged yet -- GOV_PO_3 is not marked
done until AC-5 actually runs, and this movement's own PR (once opened) does
not claim otherwise.

I have not chosen among these on my own judgment because each carries a real
cost/blast-radius trade-off (spend, first-ever unsupervised self-merge via
new infrastructure, using someone else's queued work as a test subject) that
this document's own AC-6/human-touchpoints framing reserves for a material
design/scope decision, not a routine implementation choice.
